title: The Market's Biggest Warning Signs Right Now with Todd Sohn | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 66
summary: Todd Sohn reviews stock trends, ETF flows and the concentration of index, quality and momentum exposures in technology. He favors the relative charts of Alphabet and GE Vernova, is cautious on software and several mega-caps, and warns about leveraged and thematic products. Eisman adopts the hidden-concentration lesson and emphasizes an AI-led market. Daily leverage mechanics are verified, but proprietary flow charts and stock-selection returns were not independently reproduced. Strong risk diagnosis should be separated from unproved timing and causal explanations.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Inspect underlying holdings across funds rather than count fund labels.
Separate overbought trends from automatic sell signals.
Use flows as observed positioning, not a deterministic forecast.
Distinguish daily leverage from long-horizon returns.
tools_and_charts: Relative strength and equal-weight sector returns
ETF flow percentiles and cumulative flows
Thematic maximum drawdowns and Sharpe ratios
transcript_cautions: Recording explicitly refers to June 15 despite June 29 publication.
Caption socks refers to SOXX; sharp ratio means Sharpe ratio.
Chart attachments and underlying proprietary datasets were not independently reconstructed.
Some stock-chart observations are conditional and contain no entry price, stop level or horizon.
Historical 15% industry-weight exchange is internally imprecise about which cases failed.
